key_insight: Glioblastoma necrosis may be an active, mutation-driven process in which tumor-associated neutrophil extracellular traps and HMGB2-mediated signaling amplify tumor cell necroptosis.
clinical_relevance: MRI necrotic volume and an HMGB2-high signature may support risk stratification, while the associated inflammatory cascade offers candidate therapeutic targets.
method: Integrated clinical MRI radiomics with public genomic datasets.
Mapped tumor niches using single-cell spatial transcriptomics and protein immunofluorescence.
Investigated the neutrophil–necroptosis cascade in a TP53/PTEN/NF1 co-mutant mouse model.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports public genomic datasets totaling n=3,639, multi-cohort clinical validation of the HMGB2-high signature, and mechanistic mouse-model findings, but provides no quantitative treatment effects.
watch_item: Therapeutic findings remain preclinical; the abstract does not establish human treatment benefit or describe an AI drug-discovery model.
paper_title: Tumor Associated Neutrophils Extend NETs To Spatially Drive Necroptosis In Glioblastoma
